title: Digamma reflection: psi(z)-psi(1-z) = -pi cot(pi z)
latent_structure: Master generating identity for bosonic and fermionic Matsubara kernels: the difference of digammas at reflected arguments is the cotangent thermal kernel. Differentiating in z yields polygamma reflections (DLMF 5.15.6) used for higher-order Matsubara poles. One meromorphic object (psi) plus the reflection operator z |-> 1-z.

function_domains.polygamma: psi meromorphic, poles at nonpositive integers (DLMF 5.2.2)
function_domains.tan: poles at pi*(n+1/2); 1/tan = cot has poles at n*pi

analytic_domains.statement: z and 1-z avoid the psi pole set {0,-1,-2,...}
analytic_domains.label: DERIVED
analytic_domains.source: if z not integer then neither z nor 1-z is a nonpositive integer

branch_conventions: cot = 1/tan; DLMF writes -pi/tan(pi z) equivalently -pi cot(pi z)
source_provenance: A&S 6.3.7 (DLMF notes A&S omitted the condition on z; DLMF supplies it)

derived_conditions.statement: tan(pi*z) != 0 on the same set (cot poles = integers)
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: tan(pi z)=0 iff z integer, excluded by 5.5.4

why_not_cse_lgg: Reflection of psi is a functional equation, not a shared subexpression. The latent operator is z |-> 1-z plus the cotangent kernel. CSE/LGG do not invent that operator.
proposer_leak_risk: psi and cot/tan appear in the source. Do not leak 'Matsubara master', 'thermal cotangent', or polygamma-reflection sequels in proposer context.
notes: SymPy-writable: polygamma, tan, pi. This is the generating object for thermal frequency sums; it is not a Guo identity and does not require imported pole-exclusion beyond the integers written in 5.5.4.
